BiblicalUsage: Lôʼ Dᵉbar names Lo-Debar, a place in Palestine, and its appearances in Scripture are few but pointed. In 2 Samuel 9:4, "in Lo-debar."; and in 2 Samuel 9:5, "from Lo-debar.". In 2 Samuel 17:27, "and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lo-debar".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Lo-debar is the place of the forgotten — Mephibosheth lived there lame and out of sight, until the king sent and fetched him to his own table. I hold that God fetches His people out of Lo-debar too: no place is too far for His kindness to reach.
